content: Do not take benazepril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately, as benazepril can harm the developing fetus. It belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. This medication works by reducing certain chemicals in the body that cause blood vessels to constrict, allowing blood to flow more easily. Benazepril is available in tablet form and is taken orally, usually once or twice daily, with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed; do not take more or less than directed or alter the frequency of doses. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting benazepril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to benazepril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, quinapril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially diuretics, lithium, or potassium supplements. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have recently experienced severe diarrhea or vomiting, or if you have a history of heart failure, kidney disease, lupus, scleroderma, or diabetes. If you are planning to become pregnant, are currently breastfeeding, or are scheduled for surgery (including dental procedures), inform your healthcare provider. Consult your doctor before using potassium-containing salt substitutes. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of benazepril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Benazepril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience minor side effects such as a persistent cough, headache, dizziness, or drowsiness. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; lightheadedness; fainting; rash; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or signs of infection such as fever, sore throat, or chills. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store benazepril in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness or fainting. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may also order lab tests to evaluate how your body is responding to the medication. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Benazepril is sold under the brand name Lotensin®. Combination products include Lotensin® HCT (benazepril hydrochloride and hydrochlorothiazide) and Lotrel® (benazepril hydrochloride and amlodipine besylate).
